reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes OneCoin as an appreciating asset that could provide financial freedom and directs viewers to join through a signup URL. It links sharing and network participation to a 20% bonus, highlights exceptionally large commissions, and asks viewers to invite others, despite brief acknowledgments of risk and optional recruiting.

citations.quote: When you decide to be part of the mining pools you can start as low as a hundred and thirty euros.
by submitting these tokens, will be able to generate OneCoins to your own personal account.
as you grow in death the percentage begins to decrease from eight to six to three percent that further you build your team in depth
You have the potential to earn 20% in your network and match in bonuses with your entire team.
You all want to accumulate as many ONE Coins as you can.

opening.argument: The presentation uses conditional, risk-aware language rather than promising a guaranteed outcome. It describes cryptocurrency as an investment only for someone with an appetite for “profitable risk,” and says the asset “can potentially lead” to financial freedom. It also tells listeners to get their questions answered by the person who invited them. Those qualifications matter: the speaker presents an opportunity and a personal assessment, while leaving the decision and risk with the audience. The existence of optimistic projections does not by itself establish deceptive intent or a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: It's also a good investment vehicle if you have an appetite for profitable risk.
an appreciating asset that can potentially lead yourself and your family to financial freedom.
Make sure you get all of your questions answered by the person who invited you to this call

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes the purchase price, commissions, and accumulation language, but those excerpts do not establish that any return was guaranteed. The presentation expressly describes investment as involving risk and uses “potentially,” while the cited commission passage says “potential,” not certainty. Recruitment and sharing are also presented as optional: the speaker says, “if you do decide to share this with others.” Those qualifications are material context, not irrelevant wording.

citations.quote: if you have an appetite for profitable risk.
You have the potential to earn 20% in your network and match in bonuses with your entire team.
But if you do decide to share this with others

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not neutralize the concrete sales pitch. The speaker still tells viewers they can enter mining pools for “a hundred and thirty euros,” submit tokens to generate coins, and accumulate coins as the central goal. Calling returns “potential” describes uncertainty without disclosing whether the mechanism can actually deliver them. The invitation to ask the sponsor questions also directs due diligence back to the promoter rather than providing independent verification.

opening.argument: The material is structured as an educational presentation about how cryptocurrency and blockchain work. The speaker defines cryptocurrency, explains distributed ledgers, compares them with bank databases, and describes how transactions are recorded across a network. He also calls the purpose to “educate the world” and presents an academy offering financial education. That is consistent with a technology and financial-literacy presentation: explaining a developing system and its possible applications. Promotional language may accompany an educational presentation without changing its primary subject into a proven scam.

citations.quote: Now, what is cryptocurrency? Cryptocurrency is a digital currency in which encryption techniques are used to regulate the generation of units of currency
the ledger of the cryptocurrency is the blockchain.
the blockchain is constantly synchronized across the globe as each user in the entire network has an identical copy
my intention is to educate the world as much as possible and as fast as possible

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference focuses on selected enrollment and compensation passages, but much of the presentation explains cryptocurrency concepts, payment systems, and blockchain applications. The speaker explicitly describes the subject as a cryptocurrency presentation and says the intent is education. A presenter discussing a product while explaining the underlying technology is not necessarily certifying every future projection or operating a scam.

citations.quote: our live one coin cryptocurrency presentation
The future of payments will not just be about cryptocurrency
The power of the blockchain will hold many applications in the near future

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational framing does not fit the presentation’s practical call to action. The speaker directs listeners to create an account through a sponsor, buy mining packages, receive tokens, and join recurring calls. Explaining general blockchain concepts cannot establish that this particular paid program actually performs the described mining or supports the projected value. The technology discussion functions as justification for the enrollment offer.

citations.quote: You can create a free account with the link that your sponsor has personally given you.
When you decide to be part of the mining pools you can start as low as a hundred and thirty euros.
this call will be happening every Monday and every Friday night at the same time for the next year

opening.argument: The described arrangement can be read as an ordinary paid education and digital-currency service with optional referral compensation. The speaker says there are no monthly fees, no autoship program, and no recruiting necessary to profit from the stated currency’s value. He describes a free account, an education package, and participation in mining pools, rather than asking for passwords, bank credentials, or a guaranteed deposit return. The excerpts therefore show a product and service offer with optional promotion; they do not, by themselves, establish that the service is fraudulent or that downline income is required.

citations.quote: no monthly fees no auto ship program
no recruiting necessary to profit from the value increasing in this cryptocurrency called OneCoin.
You can create a free account with the link that your sponsor has personally given you.
Whether they decide to share this opportunity or not

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited passages identify a paid mining option and optional commissions, but they do not show credential collection, a required downline, or a guaranteed payout. The speaker distinguishes the currency’s value from sharing and says members can benefit whether or not they promote it. On this record, the offer can be characterized as a digital-currency and education service with a referral program, not necessarily a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: no recruiting necessary to profit from the value increasing in this cryptocurrency called OneCoin.
Whether they decide to share this opportunity or not
on top of the One Academy

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a request for credentials is beside the point. The relevant mechanism is payment for mining-pool participation and tokens that are said to generate coins. The presentation also describes commissions tied to a team and encourages viewers to invite family and friends. Calling promotion optional does not change that the offer combines paid participation, promised coin generation, appreciation claims, and network compensation.
